- When sentiment is consistently negative (avg < -0.3) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% relative to prior peak.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 80.0), model often overshoots in next 5–7 days; cap forecast at +1.5% above spike peak or use 3-day moving average to smooth.
- If sentiment is neutral or mildly positive (avg > -0.1), model frequently overestimates; apply 1–2% downward adjustment to avoid overconfidence bias.
- Model underestimates when sentiment is strongly negative and price is trending downward; add 0.5–1.0% to forecast to account for mean reversion toward prior range.
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture late-stage sentiment-driven corrections; adjust final 5–7 days downward if sentiment turns negative within 3–5 days of forecast window.
- If sentiment history shows repeated negative spikes (e.g., 3+ consecutive negative values), model tends to ignore sentiment; apply sentiment-weighted correction: reduce forecast by 0.3–0.7x sentiment magnitude.
